$comment: Documents test-e2e-deploy.yml's NEXTJS_REF (the Next.js ref every compat cell tests) versus packages/kn-next/templates/app/package.json.hbs's next pin (the Next.js version the scaffold actually ships). tests/nextjs-credential-lockstep.test.ts fails if either real value drifts from what THIS file documents, so a future bump to either side must update this manifest in the same PR — a reviewed decision, never silent drift. As of rc.2's 16.3.5 re-credential the two are EQUAL (no more deliberate divergence) — see divergenceReason for the history and what closed it.
divergenceReason: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (2026-10-08): the scaffold ships next 16.3.8 for GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4 (HIGH, SSRF in Next.js Image Optimization, affects next >=16.0.0 <16.3.8) while the credential harness (NEXTJS_REF in test-e2e-deploy.yml) stays on v16.3.6. Moving NEXTJS_REF is a frozen-file change (the credential freeze guard covers .github/workflows/test-e2e-deploy.yml while rcTag is set) and needs an rcBumpMarker, which is founder-only; it is left for the next rc re-credential, where both sides should be made EQUAL again. The v16.3.6...v16.3.8 compare is 20 commits across 16.3.7 and 16.3.8: version bumps; next/image pinned DNS resolution for external images (image-optimizer.ts); opengraph-image dynamicParams under webpack (next-metadata-route-loader.ts); draft-mode isolation for cross-request 'use cache' dedup and metadata propagation for deduplicated nested caches (use-cache-wrapper.ts); MCP middleware DNS rebinding (get-mcp-middleware.ts); case-sensitive Next data path matching (match-next-data-pathname.ts); response-cache keys scoped to their source route (route-cache-key.ts, response-cache/index.ts, incremental-cache/index.ts, file-system-cache.ts, base-server.ts, next-server.ts, route-modules, build/adapter/build-complete.ts, export workers); a turbo-tasks-backend canceled-task read fix; a docs change to incrementalCacheHandlerPath; and test-only files. Prior history: rc.4 security bump (2026-10-01): both sides move together from 16.3.5 to 16.3.6 for GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (CRITICAL, next/og ImageResponse remote code execution, affects next >=16.2.0 <16.3.6), so they stay EQUAL. The v16.3.5...v16.3.6 compare is three commits: the version bump, a hardened next/og SVG serialization (packages/next/src/compiled/@vercel/og), and one test-only change (test/production/deterministic-build/deployment-id.test.ts) — no quarantined test file and no other runtime file moved. Next 16.3.6 keeps optionalDependencies.sharp ^0.35.4, so the sharp the harness resolves is unchanged. Earlier history: rc.2's 16.3.5 re-credential (#1560, 2026-09-30) closes the divergence rc.1 opened: NEXTJS_REF moves from v16.2.12 to v16.3.5, matching the scaffold's shipped pin. What made this possible: the six deterministic v16.3.5 failures on the four credential cells (five from the #1547/#1570 re-audit, plus one more — a webpack-only Pages API routes rewrite-query case) were triaged and found to be the vercel-infra-coupled family (ADR-0007 §h addendum) — each failing assertion sits in the test's isNextDeploy deploy branch and encodes behaviour only Vercel's own infrastructure produces, with knext's result matching the self-hosted expectation in every case — so they are evidence-quarantined, not knext gaps. Separately, the pre-existing per-case quarantine ledger (14 entries: 12 runtime-prefetch + 2 bun-edge-fetch) was re-audited with REAL dispatch evidence at v16.3.5 (all four credential cells, node/bun x turbopack/webpack, runs 36638853381/36638856495/36638859599/36638862596): of the 12 runtime-prefetch entries, 8 passed cleanly on first attempt (no retry) on all four cells and are REMOVED — their cited root-cause fix (vercel/next.js PR #95301, merge commit 97b71d0) is confirmed via the GitHub compare API to be an ancestor of v16.3.5 (compare v16.3.5...97b71d0 -> status 'behind', ahead_by 0) but NOT of v16.2.12 (status 'diverged'), which is why they were still red at the old ref and clean at the new one; the remaining 4 (prefetch-layout-sharing, segment-cache-refresh, segment-cache-per-page-dynamic-stale-time, client-cache.parallel-routes) are ALSO removed, but because upstream itself wraps them in describe.skip at v16.3.5 — they cleared by not executing, not by passing, so #95301 is not their reason. The 2 bun-edge-fetch entries were re-stamped (reaudited: v16.3.5), not removed: their documented mechanism is a Bun-runtime edge-sandbox gap independent of the Next.js ref (Bun build unchanged: 1.4.2 both times), their own history is 'cross-run wobble' (sometimes green, sometimes red) so a single clean run does not retire that class of entry, and in any case the specific cases they quarantine sit in suites.flakey and were jest-deselected in these dispatch runs — not exercised, not merely passing. NOT CLEAN AT DISPATCH TIME: the two node runs cited above (36638853381 node/turbopack, 36638856495 node/webpack) each failed knext's own bytecode-liveness gate on shards 6 and 7 — redirect-rewrite-dynamic-basepath.test.ts (shard 6) and redirect-rewrite-dynamic.test.ts (shard 7), both new-in-16.3.x upstream fixtures whose cold bake boot exceeded the driver's timeout. This was #1572 (a knext-side build-cache defect — the bake-readiness check raced a redirect response and could observe Next's own patched fetch instead of the real one), separate from the ledger re-audit above (whose test-content assertions were unaffected per each shard's own JSON). #1572 is now FIXED (#1686 — TCP readiness, manual same-origin redirect following, a captured fetch reference), proven at v16.3.5 by its own dispatch: runs 36665989345 (node/turbopack) and 36665991486 (node/webpack) show bytecode live on every shard, 0 bake failures. The node cells' clean re-credential at v16.3.5 is therefore backed by both the ledger dispatch above and the fix's proof runs. History: founder decision 2026-09-27 (#1570) cut rc.1 on v16.2.12 (the latest 16.2.x tag at or above the CVE floor 16.2.11) as the rc.1 rehearsal, deliberately deferring the harder 16.3.5 jump to rc.2 because of five upstream tests added after 16.2.x (run ids 36332940411/36332946048/36332951393/36332959885, PR #1547) — those five are the vercel-infra-coupled entries closed above. The rc.1 bump itself (v16.2.0 -> v16.2.12) was a same-minor-line re-audit of the same 14 entries (run ids on issue #1570 — runs 36348520937/36348526494/36348532038/36348537247), done in that PR, not pending.

lockstepExceptions.reason: The vinext/bun single-executable compat lane (ADR-0048, #608) is a SEPARATE axis from the four node/bun x turbopack/webpack credential cells this manifest tracks — its own credentialing is v1.x scope (not rc.1), so it is deliberately left at the pre-#1570 ref rather than silently re-pinned by this bump. Re-credential it on its own schedule, not as a side effect of the rc.1 rehearsal.

Same as the dispatch-default exception above (compat-vinext.yml) — the vinext lane's NEXTJS_REF env fallback mirrors its own dispatch default and is out of scope for the rc.1 node/bun credential rehearsal (#1570).
